1-8-cineole.name: 1,8-Cineole (Eucalyptol)
1-8-cineole.temp_notes: Highly volatile (BP 176°C); substantial loss above 65°C in open vessel

1-octen-3-ol.name: 1-Octen-3-ol
1-octen-3-ol.temp_notes: Moderate volatility (BP ~198°C); survives warm infusion at 60–65°C with modest loss

2-5-dimethylpyrazine.name: 2,5-Dimethylpyrazine
2-5-dimethylpyrazine.temp_notes: BP 155–157°C; meaningful loss in open vessel above 100°C; fat matrix of sesame paste helps retain; keep covered while cooking custard

3-bitc.name: 3-Butenyl Isothiocyanate (3-BITC)
3-bitc.temp_notes: Volatile (BP 163°C, VP 2.72 mmHg); same instability class as AITC; fat phase preferred

4-vinylguaiacol.name: 4-Vinylguaiacol (2-Methoxy-4-vinylphenol)
4-vinylguaiacol.flavor_smell: sweet, spicy, clove-like, smoky, balsamic, woody; highest OAV in roasted sesame
4-vinylguaiacol.temp_notes: BP 224°C; VP ~0.02 mmHg at 25°C — not volatile at custard temps; heat-stable through standard processing

6-msitc.name: 6-(Methylsulfinyl)hexyl Isothiocyanate (6-MSITC)
6-msitc.temp_notes: More thermally stable than AITC; survives warm infusion at 60–65°C; enzymatically generated — myrosinase must act before any heat contact

aitc.name: Allyl Isothiocyanate (AITC)

solubility.water: ~2 g/L; hydrolyzes in water → garlic off-notes

aitc.temp_notes: Volatile (BP 148°C, VP 3.7 mmHg); nearly all lost at 80°C; aqueous hydrolysis at warm temps produces garlic off-notes; cold cream only

alpha-pinene.name: α-Pinene
alpha-pinene.temp_notes: BP 156°C (313°F); lowest BP of the monoterpenes here; first to escape on heat; cold-steep only

benzyl-acetate.name: Benzyl Acetate
benzyl-acetate.temp_notes: More stable than linalool at 80°C; survives brief hot steep

beta-myrcene.name: β-Myrcene
beta-myrcene.temp_notes: BP 167°C (333°F); most volatile monoterpene in this set; lost rapidly at cooking temps; cold-steep only

cis-rose-oxide.name: cis-Rose Oxide
cis-rose-oxide.flavor_smell: rose-like, floral-green, lychee-grape; defining character compound of lychee
cis-rose-oxide.temp_notes: Stable; high BP (200.9°C); low vapor pressure — survives standard custard temps

citronellal.name: Citronellal
citronellal.temp_notes: Volatile above 75°C in open vessel; acid-sensitive — undergoes same acid-catalyzed cyclization as citral

d-limonene.name: D-Limonene
d-limonene.temp_notes: Highly volatile (BP 176°C); substantial loss above 75°C; cover infusion vessel

e-cinnamyl-acetate.name: (E)-Cinnamyl Acetate
e-cinnamyl-acetate.temp_notes: Slower to extract from bark matrix than cinnamaldehyde

ee-2-4-decadienal.name: (E,E)-2,4-Decadienal
ee-2-4-decadienal.flavor_smell: fatty, aldehydic, chicken-fat, green-melon at low concentration; OAV 1163–2015 in Sichuan peppercorn if toasted
ee-2-4-decadienal.temp_notes: Not pre-formed; generated by linoleic acid peroxidation at ≥130°C; threshold 0.07–10 ppb; light-sensitive; only relevant if pan-toasting

fenchone.name: Fenchone
fenchone.temp_notes: Volatile above 75°C (VP 0.463 mmHg, BP 192°C); keep below 75°C covered to retain

furaneol.name: Furaneol (DMHF)
furaneol.temp_notes: BP ~275°C; stable below 130°C; survives custard processing

geranial.name: Geranial (α-Citral)
geranial.temp_notes: Survives brief 80°C at neutral pH covered; acid-catalyzed cyclization to off-flavor monoterpenes — no acid before straining and cooling

geraniol.name: Geraniol
geraniol.temp_notes: BP 230°C (446°F); heat-stable through custard and boiling; acid-sensitive — converts to geranyl esters at low pH

hexanal.name: Hexanal
hexanal.temp_notes: Highly volatile (BP ~129°C); meaningful loss above 50°C; blanch plant material before processing to deactivate lipoxygenase

hydroxy-alpha-sanshool.name: Hydroxy-α-sanshool
hydroxy-alpha-sanshool.flavor_smell: tingling, numbing (má sensation); no odor; primary feel compound
hydroxy-alpha-sanshool.temp_notes: Degrades at 70°C in aqueous systems; stable in fat/oil at 50°C; acid-labile (amide group); oxidizes on storage — extract into cream fat, not water

ibmp.name: IBMP (2-Isobutyl-3-methoxypyrazine)
ibmp.flavor_smell: green pea, green bell pepper, fresh vegetal

indole.name: Indole
indole.flavor_smell: jasmine-floral at trace; fecal above threshold — dose carefully
indole.temp_notes: Highly stable; BP 253°C; concentration increases with over-steeping — 2–3 min max

linalool.name: Linalool
linalool.temp_notes: BP 194-198°C (381-388°F); partial loss during prolonged cooking above 150°C (302°F); mostly survives standard custard process at 80°C (176°F)

linalyl-acetate.name: Linalyl Acetate
linalyl-acetate.temp_notes: BP 220°C, VP 0.1 mmHg at 20°C; stable through custard processing

methional.name: Methional
methional.temp_notes: Heat-labile; decomposes rapidly above 60°C → methanethiol off-notes; negligible in cooked preparations

methyl-eugenol.name: Methyl Eugenol
methyl-eugenol.flavor_smell: warm, clove-like, sweeter and more floral than eugenol

neral.name: Neral (β-Citral)
neral.flavor_smell: softer, sweeter, more floral lemon than geranial
neral.temp_notes: Same acid/oxidation sensitivity as geranial; marginally less thermally stable; acid-catalyzed cyclization to off-flavor monoterpenes — no acid before straining

nonanal.name: Nonanal
nonanal.temp_notes: Moderate volatility (BP 195°C, VP 0.37 mmHg at 25°C); survives standard blanching

sabinene.name: Sabinene
sabinene.temp_notes: Volatile (BP 164°C, VP 2.63 mmHg); meaningful loss at 80°C; keep covered

sesamol.name: Sesamol
sesamol.flavor_smell: earthy, slightly phenolic, characteristic sesame base note
sesamol.temp_notes: BP ~228°C at atm. pressure; forms from sesamolin during high-temp roasting (>180°C); heat-stable at custard temps

trans-2-hexenal.name: Trans-2-Hexenal
trans-2-hexenal.temp_notes: Extremely volatile (VP 10 mmHg at 20°C); essentially all lost above 75–80°C; cold infusion only

trans-anethole.name: Trans-Anethole
trans-anethole.temp_notes: May crystallize in cold cream (MP 20–21°C); warm briefly to 35°C before straining

ethyl-2-methylbutanoate.name: Ethyl 2-Methylbutanoate
ethyl-2-methylbutanoate.flavor_smell: fruity, fresh, sweet apple-pineapple; defining character compound of many pineapple cultivars
ethyl-2-methylbutanoate.temp_notes: Very volatile (BP 133°C, VP ~8.8 mmHg at 20°C); substantial loss above 60°C — cold addition only to preserve

ethyl-hexanoate.name: Ethyl Hexanoate
ethyl-hexanoate.temp_notes: Moderate volatility (BP 168°C); some loss at prolonged 80°C; survives brief warm steep

delta-octalactone.name: δ-Octalactone
delta-octalactone.flavor_smell: coconut-creamy, cocoa, sweet; contributes tropical lactone note in pineapple
delta-octalactone.temp_notes: Very low volatility (BP 238°C, VP ~0.015 mmHg at 20°C); heat-stable through custard processing

ethyl-3-methylthiopropanoate.name: Ethyl 3-(Methylthio)propanoate
ethyl-3-methylthiopropanoate.flavor_smell: meaty, oniony-sulfurous, pineapple-like at low dose; savory off-note above threshold
ethyl-3-methylthiopropanoate.temp_notes: BP ~208°C (calc.); stable at custard temps; dose carefully — threshold very low

safranal.name: Safranal
safranal.flavor_smell: hay-like, iodoform, warm-metallic, characteristic saffron aroma; up to 70% of saffron's volatile fraction
safranal.temp_notes: VP 10.3 Pa at 20°C (BP 70°C at 1 mmHg ≈ 190°C atm); meaningful loss during prolonged hot infusion — steep at 60–70°C, not boiling; generated from picrocrocin during drying

lanierone.name: Lanierone (2-Hydroxy-4,4,6-trimethyl-2,5-cyclohexadien-1-one)
lanierone.flavor_smell: saffron, dried hay; highest flavor dilution factor in AEDA analysis of saffron despite lower concentration than safranal
lanierone.temp_notes: MP 56.5–57.5°C (melts in warm infusion); BP unknown; assumed moderate volatility given presence in saffron headspace

picrocrocin.name: Picrocrocin
picrocrocin.flavor_smell: intensely bitter taste; ~4% of dry saffron weight; primary taste compound; aglycone is safranal
picrocrocin.temp_notes: Stable at 80°C; degrades at 100°C with 9h half-life (>3400h at 5°C); hydrolyzes to free safranal + glucose on prolonged heating; survives standard custard cooking

crocin.name: Crocin
crocin.flavor_smell: contributes orange-red color; mild bitterness and astringency; ~6–16% of dry saffron weight; primary color marker for ISO 3632 quality grading

solubility.water: Freely soluble in hot water; sparse in cold

crocin.temp_notes: Stable; decomposes at 186°C; fat extracts essentially none — water or milk maximizes color extraction

malic-acid.name: Malic Acid
malic-acid.flavor_smell: sharp, clean sour taste; longer-lasting tartness than citric acid; primary acid responsible for sumac's characteristic sourness
malic-acid.temp_notes: Non-volatile; stable at custard temps; MP 131–133°C — fully dissolved in any warm infusion; does not volatilize

gallic-acid.name: Gallic Acid
gallic-acid.flavor_smell: bitter, astringent, drying mouthfeel (tannin character); slight fruitiness at low dose; represents the gallotannin fraction in sumac

solubility.water: ~12 g/L at 20°C; increases significantly in hot water
solubility.alcohol: Soluble (higher solubility than in water; methanol > ethanol > water)

gallic-acid.temp_notes: MP 210°C; decomposes 235–240°C; stable through custard processing; hot water extracts more than cold

p-anisaldehyde.name: p-Anisaldehyde (4-Methoxybenzaldehyde)
p-anisaldehyde.flavor_smell: sweet, anise-hawthorn, floral; distinctive aromatic modifier in sumac volatile fraction
p-anisaldehyde.temp_notes: BP 248°C, VP 0.025 mmHg at 25°C; heat-stable through custard processing

benzaldehyde.name: Benzaldehyde
benzaldehyde.flavor_smell: sweet, marzipan, bitter almond, cherry-like; defining character compound of almond extract
benzaldehyde.temp_notes: BP 179°C, VP 0.99 mmHg at 20°C; volatile above 60°C — significant loss in open vessel at custard temps; add almond extract after cooking and cooling

benzyl-alcohol.name: Benzyl Alcohol
benzyl-alcohol.flavor_smell: faintly sweet, floral, slightly almond; smooths and rounds benzaldehyde sharpness
benzyl-alcohol.temp_notes: BP 205°C, VP 13.3 mmHg at 100°C; low volatility at custard temps; slowly oxidizes in air to benzaldehyde on prolonged storage

benzoic-acid.name: Benzoic Acid
benzoic-acid.flavor_smell: faint sweet-resinous background; present in bitter almond and cherry-pit extracts
benzoic-acid.temp_notes: BP 249°C, VP 10 mmHg at 132°C; essentially non-volatile at custard temps; heat-stable

vanillin.name: Vanillin
vanillin.flavor_smell: sweet, creamy, classic vanilla; the defining character compound of cured vanilla bean
vanillin.temp_notes: BP 285°C; non-volatile at custard temps; MP 81–83°C (melts and dissolves freely in warm dairy); heat-stable — no special handling required

4-hydroxybenzaldehyde.name: 4-Hydroxybenzaldehyde (p-Hydroxybenzaldehyde)
4-hydroxybenzaldehyde.flavor_smell: sweet, floral, almond-like, slightly phenolic; second most abundant phenolic in cured vanilla
4-hydroxybenzaldehyde.temp_notes: VP 0.004 Pa at 25°C; essentially non-volatile; MP 112–116°C; heat-stable through custard processing

vanillic-acid.name: Vanillic Acid
vanillic-acid.flavor_smell: sweet vanilla, slightly phenolic, contributes depth to natural vanilla character
vanillic-acid.temp_notes: BP ~257°C; non-volatile; MP 208–210°C; heat-stable through custard processing

guaiacol.name: Guaiacol
guaiacol.flavor_smell: smoky, phenolic, woody-vanilla depth; distinguishes natural vanilla from synthetic vanillin; medicinal above threshold
guaiacol.temp_notes: BP 205°C, VP 0.11 mmHg at 25°C; low volatility — minor loss in prolonged open boil; MP 26–29°C; survives standard custard processing

alpha-terpinyl-acetate.name: α-Terpinyl Acetate
alpha-terpinyl-acetate.flavor_smell: sweet, floral, cardamom-bergamot, herbal; defining character compound of green cardamom
alpha-terpinyl-acetate.temp_notes: BP 220°C, VP 3.5 Pa at 23°C; low volatility — heat-stable through custard processing; strongly fat-soluble — extracts well into dairy fat

alpha-terpineol.name: α-Terpineol
alpha-terpineol.flavor_smell: floral, lilac, fresh pine-citrus, slightly sweet
alpha-terpineol.temp_notes: BP 217–218°C, VP 6.5 Pa at 23°C; MP 31–35°C (may solidify in cold applications); heat-stable through custard processing

decanal.name: Decanal
decanal.temp_notes: BP 207–209°C, VP ~0.15 mmHg at 20°C; strongly fat-soluble — extracts well into dairy; heat-stable through custard processing

delta-decalactone.name: δ-Decalactone
delta-decalactone.flavor_smell: sweet, creamy, peach-like, nutty; one of the defining lactone notes in ripe coconut
delta-decalactone.temp_notes: BP 117–120°C at 0.02 mmHg (very high boiling point at atmospheric pressure); heat-stable through custard processing

gamma-nonalactone.name: γ-Nonalactone
gamma-nonalactone.flavor_smell: sweet, coconut, peach-cream; characteristic lactone of coconut and ripe fruit
gamma-nonalactone.temp_notes: BP 134°C at 12 mmHg; heat-stable through custard temps

octanal.name: Octanal
octanal.flavor_smell: citrus-fatty, fresh, soapy, aldehydic; contributes bright top-note to coconut milk
octanal.temp_notes: BP 171°C, VP 1.18 mmHg at 25°C; moderate volatility — significant loss in open vessel above 80°C

ethyl-octanoate.name: Ethyl octanoate
ethyl-octanoate.flavor_smell: fruity, floral, pineapple, waxy; key ester in coconut milk contributing tropical-floral character

ethyl-decanoate.name: Ethyl decanoate
ethyl-decanoate.flavor_smell: fruity, grape, oily, floral; highest-OAV ester in raw coconut milk

ez-2-6-nonadienal.name: (E,Z)-2,6-Nonadienal
ez-2-6-nonadienal.flavor_smell: intensely fresh, green, cucumber, watermelon rind; the defining character compound of cucumber
ez-2-6-nonadienal.temp_notes: BP 94–95°C at 18 mmHg (est. ~195°C atmospheric); volatile aldehyde — cold infusion or add at end preserves maximum yield

e-2-nonenal.name: (E)-2-Nonenal
e-2-nonenal.flavor_smell: fatty, green, cucumber, citrus-waxy; second most impactful aroma compound in fresh cucumber
e-2-nonenal.temp_notes: BP 205°C at 760 mmHg; heat-stable through custard processing

ee-2-4-heptadienal.name: (E,E)-2,4-Heptadienal
ee-2-4-heptadienal.flavor_smell: fatty, fresh, green, slightly fishy; contributes fresh top-note complexity to cucumber
ee-2-4-heptadienal.temp_notes: Small volatile aldehyde (C7); treat as moderately volatile — some loss above 80°C

2-furfurylthiol.name: 2-Furfurylthiol
2-furfurylthiol.flavor_smell: intensely roasted coffee, sulfurous; odor threshold ~0.01 ppb in water — the single compound most responsible for roasted coffee smell
2-furfurylthiol.temp_notes: High boiling point (263–265°C at 17 mmHg); survives custard temps, but oxidizes rapidly in the presence of oxygen and light — freshness-sensitive; use fresh grounds or cold brew concentrate added after cooking

camphor.name: Camphor
camphor.flavor_smell: sharp, medicinal, camphorous, minty-cold; characteristic secondary note in coriander seed
camphor.temp_notes: BP 204–209°C; sublimes rather than boiling cleanly; VP 0.65 mmHg at 25°C — moderate volatility, some loss at custard temps in open vessel

e-2-decenal.name: (E)-2-Decenal
e-2-decenal.flavor_smell: waxy, citrus, coriander, fatty, aldehydic; the dominant quantitative volatile in coriander leaf essential oil; (Z) isomer has stronger fresh-coriander character at trace levels
e-2-decenal.temp_notes: BP 228–230°C at 760 mmHg; survives custard temps but may lose character at extended high heat

e-2-dodecenal.name: (E)-2-Dodecenal
e-2-dodecenal.flavor_smell: intensely aldehydic, mandarin citrus, soapy-coriander; character-impact odorant in fresh coriander leaf (GC-olfactometry top hit)
e-2-dodecenal.temp_notes: BP 93°C at 0.5 mmHg (est. ~265°C at atm); heat-stable but fresh/cold extraction maximizes yield of this character compound

beta-ionone.name: β-Ionone
beta-ionone.flavor_smell: violet, woody, fruity-raspberry, cedar; trace character-impact odorant in fresh coriander leaf
beta-ionone.temp_notes: BP 271°C at 760 mmHg; VP 0.054 mmHg at 25°C — very low volatility; heat-stable through custard processing

delta-3-carene.name: δ-3-Carene
delta-3-carene.flavor_smell: sweet, earthy, piney-citrus; dominant terpene in Ataulfo mango; turpentine-woody undertone
delta-3-carene.temp_notes: BP 168–169°C; substantial loss above 60°C in open vessel — keep mango puree cold throughout processing

terpinolene.name: Terpinolene
terpinolene.flavor_smell: fresh, sweet, piney-citrus, lemon-peel, woody; major volatile terpene in mango
terpinolene.temp_notes: BP 184–185°C; VP ~0.5 mmHg at 20°C; volatile above 65°C — cover vessel; some loss at prolonged custard temps

ethyl-butanoate.name: Ethyl Butanoate
ethyl-butanoate.flavor_smell: fruity, pineapple-orange-mango, tropical; key ester character in mango and orange
ethyl-butanoate.temp_notes: BP 120°C; extremely volatile — substantial loss above 50°C; do not heat mango puree; add after cooling if using as extract

gamma-octalactone.name: γ-Octalactone
gamma-octalactone.flavor_smell: sweet, coconut, peach, creamy-lactone; adds tropical richness to mango profile

mesifurane.name: Mesifurane (DMMF)
mesifurane.flavor_smell: musty-sweet, strawberry-jam, toffee, caramel-fruity; complements furaneol to define ripe strawberry character
mesifurane.temp_notes: BP 63°C/0.3mmHg (high atmospheric BP, est. ~200°C); relatively heat-stable; closely related to furaneol

methyl-hexanoate.name: Methyl hexanoate
methyl-hexanoate.flavor_smell: sweet, fruity, pineapple, apple, apricot; fresh top-note ester
methyl-hexanoate.temp_notes: BP 148–150°C; moderate volatility; some loss at prolonged boiling; survives brief 80°C steep

gamma-decalactone.name: Gamma-decalactone
gamma-decalactone.flavor_smell: peach, apricot, sweet, creamy, lactonic; defining peach-note compound; also present in strawberry
gamma-decalactone.temp_notes: BP 281°C at 760 mmHg; heat-stable through custard processing

zingiberene.name: Zingiberene
zingiberene.flavor_smell: spicy, characteristic ginger, herbal, slightly woody; up to 30% of ginger essential oil
zingiberene.temp_notes: BP ~255°C; heat-stable through custard processing; strongly fat-soluble — extract in cream

camphene.name: Camphene
camphene.flavor_smell: camphoraceous, piney, woody, herbal, fir-needle; cooling, citrus-adjacent terpene note in ginger
camphene.temp_notes: BP 159–162°C; volatile at cooking temps; notable loss above 80°C in open vessel

isoamyl-acetate.name: Isoamyl Acetate
isoamyl-acetate.flavor_smell: intensely banana, pear, sweet, fruity; the primary character compound of Cavendish banana and artificial banana flavor
isoamyl-acetate.temp_notes: BP 142°C, VP 5 mmHg at 25°C; highly volatile — significant loss above 60°C; do not cook banana; add cold only

isoamyl-butyrate.name: Isoamyl Butyrate
isoamyl-butyrate.flavor_smell: apricot, banana, tropical, pineapple; diffusive fruity-sweet
isoamyl-butyrate.temp_notes: BP 179°C; some loss above 80°C in open vessel; survives brief custard cooking covered

isopentyl-hexanoate.name: Isopentyl Hexanoate (Isoamyl Hexanoate)
isopentyl-hexanoate.flavor_smell: fruity, banana, apple, pineapple, green; waxy nuance
isopentyl-hexanoate.temp_notes: BP 225–226°C, VP 0.086 mmHg at 25°C; heat-stable through custard processing

isoamyl-isovalerate.name: Isoamyl Isovalerate
isoamyl-isovalerate.flavor_smell: sweet, fruity, tropical, ripe apple, jammy; green undertone
isoamyl-isovalerate.temp_notes: BP 190–191°C, VP 0.886 mmHg at 25°C; some loss above 80°C in open vessel

beta-elemene.name: β-Elemene
beta-elemene.flavor_smell: herbal, waxy, fresh; secondary sesquiterpene note in holy basil essential oil
beta-elemene.temp_notes: BP 251–253°C; heat-stable through custard processing; strongly fat-soluble

gamma-terpinene.name: γ-Terpinene
gamma-terpinene.flavor_smell: sweet, piney-citrus, herbaceous, fresh; second most abundant terpene in lime, yuzu, and buddha's hand after limonene
gamma-terpinene.temp_notes: BP 181–183°C (358–361°F); volatile above ~75°C (167°F); some loss at custard temps; cover infusion vessel

beta-pinene.name: β-Pinene
beta-pinene.flavor_smell: piney, turpentine-like, woody-fresh; citrus-herbal background note in citrus peel
beta-pinene.temp_notes: BP 166°C (331°F); volatile; meaningful loss above 65°C (149°F); keep covered

citronellol.name: Citronellol
citronellol.flavor_smell: fresh, rosy, citrus-floral; sweet rose-peach nuance; secondary floral modifier in orange and citrus peel oils
citronellol.temp_notes: BP 224°C (435°F); heat-stable through custard processing; fat-soluble

valencene.name: Valencene
valencene.flavor_smell: sweet, fresh orange, woody citrus; character-impact sesquiterpene of sweet orange (Citrus sinensis); named after Valencia orange
valencene.temp_notes: BP ~274°C (525°F) (est. atmospheric); strongly fat-soluble; heat-stable through custard processing

beta-sinensal.name: β-Sinensal
beta-sinensal.flavor_smell: intense, sweet orange aldehyde; one of the key character-impact compounds of sweet orange; aldehydic-citrus
beta-sinensal.temp_notes: BP est. ~290°C (554°F) at atm. (vacuum BP 123°C / 253°F at 11 mmHg); heat-stable; strongly fat-soluble

coumarin.name: Coumarin
coumarin.flavor_smell: pleasant vanilla-hay, bittersweet, sweet-aromatic; bitter undertone; found across citrus fruits and many herbs

methyl-benzoate.name: Methyl Benzoate
methyl-benzoate.flavor_smell: fragrant, fruity, cherry-nutty; faint orange blossom nuance in citrus context
methyl-benzoate.temp_notes: BP 199°C (390°F); moderately volatile; some loss above 80°C (176°F) in open vessel

p-cymene.name: p-Cymene
p-cymene.flavor_smell: warm, woody, thyme-like, herbaceous, slightly spicy
p-cymene.temp_notes: BP 177°C (351°F); loss during open hot infusion; some survives if vessel is covered

alpha-phellandrene.name: α-Phellandrene
alpha-phellandrene.temp_notes: BP ~171°C (340°F); volatile during hot infusion; cold-steep preferred

yuzunone.name: Yuzunone ((6Z,8E)-Undeca-6,8,10-trien-3-one)
yuzunone.flavor_smell: peely, balsamic, floral-green; defines the unique yuzu aroma; not found in other commercially traded Citrus species
yuzunone.temp_notes: BP 257–258°C (495–496°F) (est.); VP 0.015 mmHg at 25°C (77°F); heat-stable through custard processing

alpha-bisabolene.name: α-Bisabolene
alpha-bisabolene.flavor_smell: warm, herbal, slightly woody-balsamic; sesquiterpene background note in lime and citrus
alpha-bisabolene.temp_notes: BP est. ~267°C (513°F); strongly fat-soluble; heat-stable through custard processing

cis-beta-ocimene.name: cis-β-Ocimene ((Z)-β-Ocimene)
cis-beta-ocimene.flavor_smell: sweet, floral-herby, fresh citrus; herbal-green nuance; secondary terpene in citrus and basil
cis-beta-ocimene.temp_notes: BP ~176–178°C (349–352°F) (est. for cis isomer); volatile; meaningful loss above 70°C (158°F); cover vessel

limonene.name: Limonene
limonene.temp_notes: BP 175-176°C (347-349°F); significant loss in open vessel at cooking temps; cold-steep or add post-cook for maximum impact

beta-phellandrene.name: β-Phellandrene
beta-phellandrene.temp_notes: BP 171-174°C (340-345°F); volatile; same handling as α-phellandrene

elemol.name: Elemol
elemol.temp_notes: BP ~277°C (531°F); heat-stable through all standard cooking temperatures

spathulenol.name: Spathulenol
spathulenol.temp_notes: BP ~296-298°C (565-568°F); heat-stable through all standard cooking temperatures

alpha-eudesmol.name: α-Eudesmol
alpha-eudesmol.temp_notes: BP ~301°C (574°F) predicted; heat-stable through all standard cooking temperatures

beta-eudesmol.name: β-Eudesmol
beta-eudesmol.temp_notes: BP ~302°C (576°F) predicted; heat-stable through all standard cooking temperatures

gamma-eudesmol.name: γ-Eudesmol
gamma-eudesmol.temp_notes: BP ~295°C (563°F) estimated; heat-stable through all standard cooking temperatures

bicyclogermacrene.name: Bicyclogermacrene
bicyclogermacrene.temp_notes: BP ~260°C (500°F) estimated (sesquiterpene hydrocarbon); heat-stable through custard and boiling

delta-cadinene.name: δ-Cadinene
delta-cadinene.temp_notes: BP 120-121°C at 9 mmHg → ~255°C (491°F) at atmospheric pressure; heat-stable through custard and boiling

carotol.name: Carotol
carotol.temp_notes: BP ~290°C (554°F) estimated; heat-stable through all standard cooking temperatures

e-beta-ocimene.name: (E)-β-Ocimene (trans-β-Ocimene)
e-beta-ocimene.temp_notes: BP 174–175°C (345–347°F); volatile above 70°C (158°F); meaningful loss in open vessel at cooking temps

alpha-humulene.name: α-Humulene
alpha-humulene.temp_notes: BP est. ~260°C (500°F) at atm. (lit. 99–100°C at 3 mmHg); heat-stable through custard processing

caryophyllene-oxide.name: Caryophyllene Oxide (β-Caryophyllene Oxide)

delta-amorphene.name: δ-Amorphene
delta-amorphene.temp_notes: BP est. ~250°C (482°F) (C15H24 sesquiterpene structural analogy); heat-stable through custard processing

4-methylthiazole.name: 4-Methylthiazole

2-6-diethylpyrazine.name: 2,6-Diethylpyrazine
2-6-diethylpyrazine.temp_notes: BP 189–190°C (372–374°F); moderate volatility — some loss above 80°C (176°F); cover vessel during custard cooking

2-ethyl-6-methylpyrazine.name: 2-Ethyl-6-methylpyrazine

3-methylbutanal.name: 3-Methylbutanal (Isovaleraldehyde)

syringol.name: Syringol (2,6-Dimethoxyphenol)

fenchyl-acetate.name: Fenchyl Acetate (1,3,3-Trimethyl-2-norbornyl Acetate)

beta-sesquiphellandrene.name: (+)-beta-Sesquiphellandrene

ar-curcumene.name: ar-Curcumene (alpha-Curcumene)

trans-beta-ocimene.name: (E)-beta-Ocimene (trans-beta-Ocimene)

isoamyl-propanoate.name: Isoamyl Propanoate (Isoamyl Propionate)

methyl-butanoate.name: Methyl Butanoate (Methyl Butyrate)
